issues.legal_issue: A retrospective validating enactment that does not disclose the amendments to the underlying law does not validate an enhanced levy that required prior governmental sanction.
material_facts: An earlier court ruling held that increases to a cess required prior governmental sanction and that the enhanced rates were unlawful because that sanction had not been obtained.
A later enactment deemed cess imposed under specified notices to have been validly imposed as if the underlying enactment had been amended, but did not state the text or nature of any amendment.
The enactment was confined to one local body and the specified notices; it did not expressly provide that notices issued without sanction were valid.
issues.conclusion: The later enactment did not give legal effect to the enhanced cess levies.
issues.legal_principle: A taxing enactment must be interpreted according to its clear language: nothing is to be read in or implied, as stated in Cape Brandy Syndicate v. Commissioners of Inland Revenue and approved in Canadian Eagle Oil Co. Ltd. v. King and applied by this Court in Commissioner of Income-tax v. Ajax Products Ltd. and Commissioner of Income-tax v. B. M. Kharwar. Although a legislature may, within limits, amend law retrospectively, the Madhya Pradesh Koyala Upkar (Manyatakaran) Adhiniyam, 1964, section 3(1), did not identify an amendment to the Central Provinces Local Self-Government Act, 1920, section 51(2), that removed the prior-sanction requirement or otherwise validated the notices. Its limited scope did not repeal that generally applicable requirement by implication.

rule.if: validation_challenge and prior_court_found_enhancement_unlawful and later_law_deems_levy_valid_as_if_amended and amendment_content_unspecified and law_limited_to_specific_body_and_notices

predicates.validation_challenge: The proceeding challenges whether a later validating law cured an enhanced levy previously held unlawful.
predicates.prior_court_found_enhancement_unlawful: A court held that an enhanced levy was unlawful because a required prior governmental sanction had not been obtained.
predicates.later_law_deems_levy_valid_as_if_amended: A later law purports to deem the levy valid as if the underlying law had been amended.
predicates.amendment_content_unspecified: The later law does not state the text or nature of the amendment that would make the levy valid.
predicates.law_limited_to_specific_body_and_notices: The later law applies only to a particular local body and specified notices rather than generally changing the underlying requirement.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns a levy previously held unlawful, a later law that deems it valid without specifying a necessary amendment and applies only to a particular body and notices leaves the enhanced levy unvalidated.

issues.legal_issue: A legislature cannot make a properly rendered judicial judgment ineffective merely by declaring that it is ineffective.
material_facts: A court had held that the enhanced levy was unlawful because prior governmental sanction had not been obtained.

The later enactment purported to operate notwithstanding a court judgment and to deem the specified levies valid, without disclosing a substantive amendment that removed the defect identified by the court.
The judgment had been rendered by a properly constituted court in a matter before it and declared the law governing the levy.
issues.conclusion: The legislature could not render the earlier judgment ineffective, either as a precedent or between the parties, by the terms of the later enactment.
issues.legal_principle: A legislature may, within constitutional limits, retrospectively amend the law and declare what the law is deemed to have been; it may not simply declare ineffective a judgment properly rendered by a court or displace the court's declaration of law. The earlier decision in The Amalgamated Coalfields Ltd. v. The Janapada Sabha, Chhindwara was binding between the parties and, under Article 141 of the Constitution, on all courts in India.

rule.if: legislative_override_challenge and properly_rendered_judgment_exists and enactment_declares_judgment_ineffective and underlying_legal_defect_not_removed

predicates.legislative_override_challenge: The proceeding challenges a legislative enactment that purports to overcome a judicial judgment.
predicates.properly_rendered_judgment_exists: A properly constituted court has rendered a judgment in a matter before it and declared the governing law.
predicates.enactment_declares_judgment_ineffective: The enactment purports to make the judgment ineffective.
predicates.underlying_legal_defect_not_removed: The enactment does not substantively change the law in a way that removes the defect identified in the judgment.

issues.definition: When an enactment declares a properly rendered judgment ineffective without removing the underlying legal defect, the legislature cannot make that judgment ineffective.
